READING

**Step 1 – Financial arithmetic, properly stated**

The KESTERWICK case as presented quotes £96,000/year of rent saving against £480,000 of works and says you are "clear" after ten years. That omits the dead mileage cost.

Culverstone is 3 miles further from Verrancombe Bridge. The 44-network vehicles leave the depot dead and return dead, so the extra movement per vehicle per day is 6 miles (out and back).

22 vehicles × 313 days × 6 miles × £0.63 = **£26,029/year extra running cost**

Net annual saving, KESTERWICK over ARDENSHAW: £96,000 − £26,029 = **£69,971**

Upfront cash cost of KESTERWICK: £480,000 works + £40,000 non-refundable deposit = **£520,000**

Break-even: £520,000 ÷ £69,971 = **7.4 years** into the ten-year term

Net financial benefit of KESTERWICK if everything goes perfectly: roughly £180,000 over the full ten years. That is real money but is not the transformational figure the KESTERWICK framing implies.

**Step 2 – Planning timeline laid out against the critical dates**

Application validated: 2026-08-14. From that date:

| Scenario | Weeks | Approx consent | + 22 weeks works | Ready by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target | 13 | 2026-11-13 | 2027-04-01 | ✓ before bid, before lease-end |
| Median | 34 | 2027-04-10 | 2027-08-28 | ✓ 17 days before bid deadline; 3 months before lease-end |
| Slowest recorded | 61 | 2027-10-15 | 2028-03-20 | ✗ consent after bid, move-in after lease-end |

Two external deadlines constrain KESTERWICK:
- **44/44A bid due 2027-09-14.** For Culverstone to be built and occupiable before bid day, consent must arrive by approximately 2027-04-14. That is 34 weeks from validation — exactly the median.
- **Hallowbrand lease ends 2027-11-30.** Consent must arrive by roughly 2027-06-29 (47 weeks) for works to complete before then. That is well inside the worst-case 61 weeks but only two-thirds of the way through the range.

The planning authority's ratio of median-to-target is 34:13 = **2.6×**. When an authority routinely takes 2.6 times its own published target, its distribution is wide and right-skewed. You cannot treat the median as "likely" in the way you would if the authority were normally distributed around the target.

**Step 3 – The bid is the load-bearing beam**

"Depot cost goes into the bid as a fixed line." The 44/44A contract runs 22 of 31 vehicles and presumably anchors the business. The next term is from 2028-04-01; bid day is 2027-09-14.

*At the median determination (34 weeks):* Consent arrives ~10 April 2027. Works complete ~28 August 2027. You enter the bid on ~14 September 2027 with Culverstone operational. Depot line: £118,000 + dead mileage. This is fine — but the margin is 17 days. Any single slip beyond the median destroys it.

*Beyond the median:* You must submit the bid either with no confirmed depot (planning still live, works not started) or with Nethercote's costs. Nethercote is £18,500/month = **£222,000/year** — which is *more* than ARDENSHAW's £214,000. Bidding from Nethercote means you price the contract *worse* than if you had simply signed at Hallowbrand, while having sacrificed the Hallowbrand offer and paid a non-refundable deposit. The competitive advantage of KESTERWICK in the bid turns into a competitive disadvantage.

By definition, outcomes worse than the median happen in half or more of all cases. This planning authority's record makes it imprudent to treat the median as the planning case.

**Step 4 – Worst-case walkthrough**

Consent: ~2027-10-15. Works complete: ~2028-03-20.

Hallowbrand expires 2027-11-30. Nethercote from ~1 December 2027 to ~20 March 2028 ≈ 3.7 months = **c.£68,000** at £18,500/month, with no workshop. School contracts and private hire must find maintenance access elsewhere. The 44/44A contract ends 2028-03-31, just as Culverstone becomes usable — meaning the entire next tender term (from April 2028) would in principle be operated from Culverstone, but you have bid it blind in September 2027.

**Step 5 – Planning refusal risk**

The problem does not state the probability of refusal but it is not zero. If consent is refused after the £40,000 deposit is paid and the Hallowbrand deadline has passed (2026-12-19), Trentmoor has no depot from November 2027, a landlord who knows it, a non-refundable outlay already spent, and a live contract bid. That is an existential exposure. ARDENSHAW carries no comparable tail risk.

**Step 6 – Cash position**

Under KESTERWICK: £640,000 − £40,000 − £480,000 = £120,000 residual cash plus £200,000 facility = £320,000 headroom during the construction and transition window, which may also include Nethercote costs and any works overrun. Workable, but thin going into a period when the 44/44A bid must be funded and delivered.

Under ARDENSHAW: cash largely intact, facility undrawn, no construction exposure.

**Step 7 – What would make KESTERWICK the better call**

The KESTERWICK case would be compelling if the planning authority hit anywhere near its 13-week target (consent would be available months ahead of all critical dates), or if the bid deadline were post-April 2028 (giving the full 61-week slow case room to resolve), or if the financial saving were larger. None of those conditions holds. The authority is running at 2.6× its own target at the median; the bid falls at exactly the median determination date; and the net saving is £70,000/year against break-even at year 7.4.

**Conclusion**

ARDENSHAW costs £69,971/year more in net terms and locks the business into Hallowbrand until 2037. Those are real disadvantages. But it delivers the September 2027 bid with a depot cost known to the penny, eliminates planning refusal risk, preserves workshop continuity, and keeps the balance sheet healthy. KESTERWICK's financial case depends on a planning outcome at or better than the median of an authority running at 2.6× its published target, with the bid date as the tripwire. The cost of being wrong under KESTERWICK — a mispriced or forfeited contract renewal driving 22 of 31 vehicles — dwarfs the £180,000 best-case saving over ten years.

READING

The above constitutes my full working.

CALL
ARDENSHAW

GROUNDS
The September 2027 bid deadline falls at exactly the median planning determination time for an authority running at 2.6× its own published target, so there is roughly an even chance that the 44/44A renewal must be priced from Nethercote at £222,000 a year or with no confirmed depot at all, a competitive outcome worse than ARDENSHAW and one that would erase the entire ten-year rent saving many times over.
